scope: A basement additional residential unit (ARU) inside an existing detached, semi-detached or row house anywhere in Ontario, using the rules that apply across the province. Your municipality's own zoning by-law, fees, grants and forms are not in this pack.
disclaimer: Screening aid only. Not legal, building-code, tax or financial advice, and not a permit decision. These are Ontario's province-wide rules; your municipality's zoning by-law and building department decide for your lot. Costs are estimates, not quotes.

codeInForce.regulation: O. Reg. 163/24 (Building Code) under the Building Code Act, 1992. Reg. 325/26, filed 2026-10-02).

Reg. 163/24, s. 2). A permit applied for now uses the 2024 Code.

existingBuildings.rule: Part 11 (Renovation) applies to buildings, or parts of buildings, that have been in existence for at least five years. Its compliance alternatives (Table 11.5.1.1.-C for residential) may replace Part 9 requirements without the chief building official having to find compliance impracticable.

source.title: 2024 Building Code Compendium, Division A Part 1

relatedSources.title: 2024 Building Code Compendium, Division B Part 11

secondarySuiteDefinition.text: A secondary suite is a self-contained dwelling unit in a building of only residential occupancy that contains only one other dwelling unit and common spaces, where both units form a single real estate entity (one title).
secondarySuiteDefinition.implication: The Code's 'house with a secondary suite' provisions used in this pack apply only when the house has exactly two dwelling units. A third unit inside the house (which the Planning Act allows) takes the building outside that definition; the pack does not cover the three-unit case.

source.title: 2024 Building Code Compendium, Division A Part 1

codeInForce.notes: Not reviewed: what the October 1, 2026 amendment document (O. Reg. 325/26) changed, because the compendium HTML is current only to O. Reg. 242/26. Ontario's 'Add a second unit to your house' guide (updated 2023-01-30) still cites 2012 Code numbers (e.g. C.A. 102, 136, 147, 195); this pack uses the 2024 numbers.

routes.summary: Finish the basement as more living space for the existing home. It stays one dwelling unit, so the two-household rules (fire separation between units, interconnected alarms between units, sound, HVAC separation) don't apply; the normal Part 9 rules for one home do, such as a bedroom escape window, a smoke alarm on every storey and ceiling heights.
routes.permit: A building permit from your municipality; the fee is set by its fees by-law.

sources.title: Add a second unit in your house (Government of Ontario, updated 2023-01-30)

routes.summary: Create an additional residential unit: a separate home with its own kitchen, bathroom and living and sleeping space. Ontario's Planning Act s. 35.1 stops zoning from banning up to 3 homes in the house on a serviced residential lot, from asking for more than one parking space per additional home, or from setting a minimum unit size. It needs a building permit, the Code's 'house with a secondary suite' rules and an ESA permit.
routes.permit: A building permit from your municipality on Ontario's application form; the fee is set by its fees by-law. The Code gives 15 business days to decide a complete application for a house with one home above another (Div. C Table 1.3.1.3).
routes.appliesRules: all rules whose route includes second_unit

sources.title: Planning Act, R.S.O. 1990, c. P.13 (consolidation from 2026-07-01)
2024 Building Code Compendium (MMAH), Division C Part 1

rules.title: Up to three homes in the house
rules.plain: Ontario stops zoning from banning a second or third home inside a detached, semi-detached or row house, on a lot with municipal water and sewer where houses are allowed. Your municipality may allow more.

evidence.question: How many separate homes (each with its own kitchen and bathroom) are in the house now, and is there one in a garage or backyard building?

fix.description: If the house already has three homes, or two plus one out back, Ontario's rule doesn't cover another one. Ask your municipality, or finish the basement as part of an existing home.

source.title: Planning Act, R.S.O. 1990, c. P.13 (consolidation from 2026-07-01)

relatedSources.title: O. Reg. 299/19: Additional Residential Units (consolidation from 2024-11-20)
relatedSources.section: s. 1(2) paras 1-2; s. 2 para 5 (any date of construction)

relatedSources.title: List of Ontario municipalities (Government of Ontario, updated 2026-06-03)

rules.notes: Applies on a 'parcel of urban residential land' (Planning Act s. 1(1)): in a settlement area, where houses are allowed, served by municipal sewage works and a municipal drinking water system. The Building Code's 'house with a secondary suite' rules cover a house with exactly two units.

rules.title: On municipal water and sewer
rules.plain: Ontario's three-unit rule covers lots on municipal sewers and a municipal water system. On a well or a septic system, your municipality's zoning decides.

evidence.question: Is the house on municipal water and sewer (not a private well or septic system)?

fix.description: On a well or septic system the provincial rule doesn't apply. Ask your municipality whether its zoning allows a second unit on your lot.

source.title: Planning Act, R.S.O. 1990, c. P.13 (consolidation from 2026-07-01)
source.section: s. 1(1) definition of 'parcel of urban residential land'

relatedSources.title: Planning Act, R.S.O. 1990, c. P.13 (consolidation from 2026-07-01)

rules.notes: Not a ban: off municipal services, the Planning Act simply doesn't guarantee the units, so the local zoning by-law decides.

rules.title: At most one parking space for the new home
rules.plain: Zoning can't ask for more than one parking space for each additional home, and that space may be one behind another in the driveway. Where the main house needs no space, the new home needs none.

check.appliesWhen: the zoning by-law requires a space for the main home and doesn't waive it for additional units

evidence.question: Is there room for one more car on your driveway, even parked one behind another?

fix.description: Ask your municipality whether its zoning needs a space for the new home; if it does, one tandem space in the driveway is enough.

source.title: O. Reg. 299/19: Additional Residential Units (consolidation from 2024-11-20)
source.section: s. 2 paras 1-3; s. 3 (a by-law that requires no space prevails)

relatedSources.title: Planning Act, R.S.O. 1990, c. P.13 (consolidation from 2026-07-01)
relatedSources.section: s. 35.1(1.1) (no more than one space per additional unit)

rules.notes: O. Reg. 299/19 also says anyone may live in either home, related or not, and the owner doesn't have to live there (s. 2 para 4), and zoning can't set a minimum size for the unit (Planning Act s. 35.1(1.2)).

rules.title: Ceiling height in the suite: 1.95 m
rules.plain: Ceilings in the new suite must be at least 1.95 m high, and the areas that meet the height must connect to each room's entrance.

evidence.scanMeasurement: Finished floor to finished ceiling in every room of the planned suite; flag areas under 1.95 m and check they are not between the entrance and the rest of the room.
evidence.question: What is the lowest floor-to-ceiling height in the rooms you plan for the suite, after flooring and drywall?

fix.description: Lower the floor (underpinning or bench footings, needs an engineer) or reduce finishes; ceiling-height fixes were not priced in this pack.

source.title: 2024 Building Code Compendium (MMAH), Division B

rules.notes: Part 11 compliance alternative C105 (1,950 mm / 2,030 mm) expressly excludes secondary suites, because 9.5.3.1.(2)-(3) already set lower heights for suites, so no further relaxation applies to existing houses. A scan of an unfinished basement measures to the joists: subtract planned flooring and the 15.9 mm Type X ceiling.

rules.title: Clearance under beams and ducts: 1.85 m
rules.plain: Under beams and ductwork inside the suite, the clear height must be at least 1.85 m.

evidence.scanMeasurement: Finished floor to the underside of each beam, duct or bulkhead after finishes.
evidence.question: What is the lowest clearance under any beam or duct in the planned suite?

fix.description: Reroute or flatten ductwork into joist spaces, or relocate the suite's main paths away from low beams; not priced in this pack.

source.title: 2024 Building Code Compendium (MMAH), Division B

rules.title: Ceiling height if it stays part of the house
rules.plain: Finishing the basement as part of the main home: basement space needs 2.1 m over at least 75% of its area (1.95 m under beams and ducts); in a house 5+ years old, finished rooms may instead have 1.95 m over the required floor area and exit paths, or 2.03 m over at least half of it.

orCheck.note: floor under 1,400 mm high is not counted in the required area

source.title: 2024 Building Code Compendium, Division B Part 11

evidence.scanMeasurement: Finished ceiling height across the basement; share of area at or above 2.1 m; clearance under beams and ducts.
evidence.question: Roughly how high is the basement ceiling, and how low are the beams and ducts?

fix.description: Usually none needed for an existing house that meets 1.95 m; otherwise see ceiling_height_suite fixes.

source.title: 2024 Building Code Compendium (MMAH), Division B

rules.notes: Finished rooms such as bedrooms and living rooms follow their own rows of Table 9.5.3.1. C105 says 'Except for secondary suites', so it is the basement-finish route that uses it. For houses 5+ years old, the suite (1.95 m, 1.85 m under beams) and the basement finish (1.95 m) end up close.

rules.title: Bedroom escape window: 0.35 m² opening
rules.plain: Every floor level with a bedroom needs at least one outside window that opens from inside without tools, stays open by itself and gives an unobstructed opening of at least 0.35 m², unless that level has a door straight to the outside.

existingBuildingAlternative.text: In a single dwelling unit or a house with a secondary suite, existing [bedroom egress] acceptable, where there is direct access to the exterior.

source.title: 2024 Building Code Compendium, Division B Part 11

existingBuildingAlternative.interpretationNote: The Code does not say whether 'direct access to the exterior' is from the bedroom, the floor level or the suite. Treat as 'ask the building department'; do not auto-pass.

evidence.scanMeasurement: Clear opening width and height of the openable sash (not the frame), multiplied for area.
evidence.question: For each window on the bedroom level: what type is it (casement, slider, awning, hopper) and how wide and tall is the opening when fully open?

fix.description: Cut and enlarge the foundation opening and install an egress-size window with a code-compliant window well.

costSource.title: Basement Renovation Cost Guide: Kitchener-Waterloo & Cambridge 2026

fix.costNote: Estimate, not a quote. Waterloo Region contractor guide. HomeStars (Canada) gives $3,500-$8,000 for a new opening with window and well; a Toronto source gives $7,500-$17,000. See costs[].

source.title: 2024 Building Code Compendium (MMAH), Division B

rules.notes: Passing needs both this rule and egress_window_min_dimension: a 380 x 380 mm opening meets the dimension but fails the area (Note A-9.9.10.1.(1)). The rule is per floor level containing a bedroom in a suite. The wording 'except where a door on the same floor level as the bedroom provides direct access to the exterior' means a walkout door on that level satisfies it.

rules.title: Bedroom escape window: no side under 380 mm
rules.plain: The escape window's clear opening must be at least 380 mm in every direction; for sliders, measure only the part that opens.

existingBuildingAlternative.text: In a single dwelling unit or a house with a secondary suite, existing [bedroom egress] acceptable, where there is direct access to the exterior.

source.title: 2024 Building Code Compendium, Division B Part 11

existingBuildingAlternative.interpretationNote: The Code does not say whether 'direct access to the exterior' is from the bedroom, the floor level or the suite. Treat as 'ask the building department'; do not auto-pass.

evidence.scanMeasurement: Smaller of clear opening width and height of the openable portion.
evidence.question: When the window is fully open, how wide and how tall is the clear gap?

fix.description: Same as egress_window_bedroom_area (larger window, possibly a casement).

costSource.title: Basement Renovation Cost Guide: Kitchener-Waterloo & Cambridge 2026

fix.costNote: Estimate, not a quote; shared with the window enlargement fix.

source.title: 2024 Building Code Compendium (MMAH), Division B

rules.title: Window well: 550 mm clear in front
rules.plain: If the escape window opens into a window well, keep at least 550 mm clear in front of it (beyond any outward-opening sash), and any well cover must open from inside without keys or tools.

existingBuildingAlternative.text: In a single dwelling unit or a house with a secondary suite, existing [bedroom egress] acceptable, where there is direct access to the exterior.

source.title: 2024 Building Code Compendium, Division B Part 11

existingBuildingAlternative.interpretationNote: The Code does not say whether 'direct access to the exterior' is from the bedroom, the floor level or the suite. Treat as 'ask the building department'; do not auto-pass.

evidence.scanMeasurement: Horizontal distance from the window (or the outer edge of an outward-opening sash) to the inside face of the well.
evidence.question: Does the bedroom window open into a window well? How far is it from the glass to the well wall, and is there a cover?

fix.description: Replace the well with a deeper/wider one (usually done with the window enlargement) and use an inside-openable cover.
fix.costNote: Included in the egress window enlargement ranges in costs[]; no separate price found.

source.title: 2024 Building Code Compendium (MMAH), Division B

rules.notes: Note A-9.9.10.1.(3) advises allowing for snow in the well and says hopper (bottom-hinged) windows should not be used where occupants must climb over the glass.

rules.title: Escape window sill height (advice for basements)
rules.plain: There is no maximum sill height for basement escape windows, but the Code's explanatory note recommends a sill no higher than 1.5 m above the floor, or built-in furniture or a step below it. Above-grade bedroom levels must have a sill at most 1,000 mm high.

evidence.scanMeasurement: Floor to the bottom of the clear opening.
evidence.question: How high is the bottom of the window opening above the floor?

fix.description: Add a fixed step or built-in furniture under the window, or lower the opening during enlargement.

source.title: 2024 Building Code Compendium (MMAH), Division B

rules.notes: Advisory only for basements: 9.9.10.1.(2) exempts basement areas from the 1,000 mm maximum; the 1.5 m figure is a recommendation in Appendix A, not a requirement.

rules.title: Fire/smoke separation between the two homes
rules.plain: Separate the suite from the rest of the house with a 45-minute fire separation, or with a continuous smoke-tight barrier of 15.9 mm (5/8 in.) Type X drywall on both sides of dividing walls and under the floor/ceiling framing. The rating can be waived if the house is sprinklered.

options: In a house with a secondary suite, a 15 min horizontal fire separation is acceptable where smoke alarms are installed in every dwelling unit and in common areas in conformance with Subsection 9.10.19. and are interconnected
In a house with a secondary suite, the fire-resistance rating of the fire separation is waived where the building is sprinklered throughout

source.title: 2024 Building Code Compendium, Division B Part 11

evidence.question: Is the basement ceiling open (joists visible) or drywalled? If drywalled, do you know the type and thickness (e.g. 1/2 in. regular or 5/8 in. Type X)? Is there a door between the basement and the upstairs home?

fix.description: Install 5/8 in. Type X drywall on the suite ceiling and on both sides of dividing walls, keep it continuous and seal joints and penetrations; add self-closing doors where the separation has openings.

costSource.title: Cost to Make a Basement Legal in Toronto

fix.costNote: Estimate, not a quote (Toronto, 2026, 'fire separation' line). Ceiling drywall installed and finished is $4.00-$6.50/sq ft before the Type X upgrade (see costs[]).

source.title: 2024 Building Code Compendium (MMAH), Division B

relatedSources.title: 2024 Building Code Compendium (MMAH), Division B
relatedSources.section: Table 11.5.1.1.-C, C160 (existing 45 mm solid-core doors acceptable)

rules.notes: The 15 min option for existing houses only works together with interconnected smoke alarms in both units and common areas. Lath-and-plaster or existing drywall may already give 15 minutes; that needs the building department or a designer to confirm.

rules.title: Protect beams and posts that hold up the floor between units
rules.plain: Light-frame walls, columns and beams, and loadbearing steel, that support the floor between the two units must be covered with 15.9 mm (5/8 in.) Type X drywall.

options: In a house with a secondary suite, 15 min horizontal fire separation is acceptable where smoke alarms are installed in every dwelling unit and in common areas and are interconnected
In a house with a secondary suite, the fire-resistance rating is waived where the building is sprinklered throughout

source.title: 2024 Building Code Compendium, Division B Part 11

evidence.question: Are the main basement beam and posts steel or wood, and are they exposed?

fix.description: Box in the beam and posts with 5/8 in. Type X drywall (usually done with the fire-separation ceiling).
fix.costNote: No separate price found; normally part of the fire separation job.

source.title: 2024 Building Code Compendium (MMAH), Division B

relatedSources.title: 2024 Building Code Compendium, Appendix A
relatedSources.section: Note A-9.10.8.3.(2) (light-frame excludes heavy timber, masonry, concrete)

rules.title: Furnace room separation
rules.plain: If the furnace or water heater serves both units, put it in a service room lined with 15.9 mm (5/8 in.) Type X drywall on both sides of its walls and on the underside of the ceiling framing; otherwise fuel-fired appliances need a 1-hour fire separation.

check.appliesWhen: a fuel-fired appliance serves both dwelling units

options: In a house with a secondary suite, the fire-resistance rating of the vertical fire separation is waived where smoke alarms are installed in every dwelling unit and in common areas and are interconnected
In a house with a secondary suite, the fire-resistance rating of the vertical fire separation is waived where service rooms are sprinklered

source.title: 2024 Building Code Compendium, Division B Part 11

evidence.question: Is the furnace or water heater in its own enclosed room? Will it serve both homes, and which unit would the room open into?

fix.description: Enclose the furnace/water heater in its own room and line its walls (both sides) and ceiling with 5/8 in. Type X drywall.
fix.costNote: No separate price found; usually part of the fire separation work.

source.title: 2024 Building Code Compendium (MMAH), Division B

rules.notes: C157 waives only the vertical (wall) rating; the ceiling still needs separation. 9.10.10.4.(2)(a) also exempts appliances that serve only one room or suite.

rules.title: Interconnected smoke alarms in both homes
rules.plain: Put smoke alarms on every storey, in every bedroom and outside sleeping areas of each unit, and in shared exits and common areas, then interconnect them (hard-wired or wireless) so any one alarm sounds all alarms in both homes.

existingBuildingAlternative.text: Smoke alarms may be battery operated.
existingBuildingAlternative.note: Interconnection under 9.10.19.5.(2) is still required; wireless interconnection is allowed.

source.title: 2024 Building Code Compendium, Division B Part 11

evidence.question: Is there a smoke alarm on every level and in each bedroom? When you test one, do all the others sound, including in the other home?

fix.description: Install interconnected smoke alarms (hard-wired or wireless) with a visual (strobe) signal in both units and common areas.
fix.costNote: No standalone Ontario price found; one Toronto source bundles alarms into a $4,000-$8,000 electrical line (see costs[]).

source.title: 2024 Building Code Compendium (MMAH), Division B

rules.notes: The 2024 Code also requires a visual signalling component (NFPA 72 s. 18.5.3; at least 175 cd in sleeping rooms). Part 11 gives no specific alternative for the strobe; how building departments apply it to conversions was not confirmed. Note A-9.10.19.5.(2): units with separate electrical services can interconnect wirelessly.

rules.title: Interconnected carbon monoxide alarms
rules.plain: If the house has a fuel-burning appliance (such as a gas furnace or water heater) or an attached garage, put CO alarms next to the sleeping rooms in each unit and in the service room, interconnected so one alarm sounds all CO alarms in the house.

existingBuildingAlternative.text: Carbon monoxide alarms may be battery operated or plugged into an electrical outlet.

source.title: 2024 Building Code Compendium, Division B Part 11

evidence.question: Is the furnace or water heater gas, oil or propane? Are there CO alarms near the bedrooms in both homes, and do they sound together?

fix.description: Add CO alarms beside each sleeping area in both units and in the furnace room, interconnected across the house.

source.title: 2024 Building Code Compendium (MMAH), Division B
source.section: 9.32.3.9C.(1) (interconnection within a house with a secondary suite)

rules.notes: The compendium HTML does not show clause letters for 9.32.3.9C., so the citation is at Sentence level. 9.32.3.9C. also requires a visual signalling component.

rules.title: A safe way out of the suite
rules.plain: Best: the suite has its own door to the outside. A shared exit is allowed if it is separated by a 30-minute fire separation, does not pass through the other home or a service room, and both homes have interconnected smoke alarms. Leaving through the other home is only allowed with an extra escape window and interconnected alarms, or if the house is sprinklered.

options: (a) own_exterior_door: a door (including a sliding door) that opens directly to the exterior from the dwelling unit, serves only that unit, has reasonable access to ground level, and the units have smoke alarms per 9.10.19

(b) shared_exit_30min_separated: an exit accessible to more than one unit that is the only means of egress, separated from the rest of the building and common areas by a 30 min fire separation; access to it may not pass through another unit, a service room or another occupancy; both units and common areas have interconnected smoke alarms

(c) through_other_unit_plus_escape_window: access to exit leads through the other unit and an extra escape window is provided: sill not more than 1,000 mm above or below adjacent ground, openable without tools, opening at least 0.38 m2 with no dimension under 460 mm, sill not more than 900 mm above the floor or fixed steps, and at least 1,000 mm clear in a window well; interconnected smoke alarms in every unit and common area
(c-alt) upper-floor escape window: casement at least 1,060 mm high and 560 mm wide, sill not more than 900 mm above the inside floor and not more than 5 m above ground; interconnected smoke alarms
(d) sprinklered: the building is sprinklered and the units have smoke alarms per 9.10.19

source.title: 2024 Building Code Compendium, Division B Part 11

evidence.question: In a fire, how would someone leave the basement home: its own door to the outside, a shared stair or hall to an outside door, or only through the upstairs home?

fix.description: Add a separate entrance (side or rear walk-up/walk-out), or enclose the shared stair with a 30-minute fire separation and self-closing door.

costSource.title: Basement Apartment Legalization Toronto: 2026 Code, Egress, Ceiling Height, Fire Separation

fix.costNote: Estimate, not a quote (Toronto, separate side entry). A simpler at-grade door is $5,000-$10,000+ (RenoQuotes). See costs[].

source.title: 2024 Building Code Compendium, Division B Part 11

relatedSources.title: Add a second unit to your house

rules.notes: Option labels (a)-(d) are this pack's names for the C139 conditions in the order printed. For houses under 5 years old the base Part 9 exit rules apply and are not mapped in this pack; ask the building department.

rules.title: No shared air between the homes
rules.plain: Each home's air ducts may not be directly connected to the other home, and air from one suite may not be recirculated to the other. In a house 5+ years old, one existing forced-air system may serve both if each unit has smoke alarms and a duct smoke detector shuts off the furnace's fuel and power when it detects smoke.

existingBuildingAlternative.ref: Table 11.5.1.1.-C, compliance alternatives C201 (for 9.33.1.1.) and C97 (for 6.3.2.7.(1)); C172 (for 9.10.13.13.(1))
existingBuildingAlternative.text: In a building containing not more than four dwelling units, the existing heating or air-conditioning system may be altered to serve more than one dwelling unit, provided smoke alarms are installed in each dwelling unit and a smoke detector is installed in the supply or return air duct system serving the entire building which would turn off the fuel supply and electrical power to the heating system upon activation of such detector.
existingBuildingAlternative.fireDampers: C172: in houses with a secondary suite, existing [duct penetrations without fire dampers] acceptable.

source.title: 2024 Building Code Compendium, Division B Part 11

evidence.question: Does one furnace heat both floors? Are there return-air grilles in the basement that pull air back to the shared furnace?

fix.description: Existing house: add a duct-type smoke detector interlocked to shut the furnace's fuel and power. Or give the suite its own heating (separate furnace or ductless heat pump) and seal the duct connections between units.

costSource.title: How Much Does Basement Development Cost in Canada in 2026?
costSource.note: Read via the r.homestars.com mirror of the same path.

fix.costNote: Estimate, not a quote, for an independent heating system. Ductless mini-split $3,500-$7,000; firestop and fire dampers $1,000-$3,000. No price found for a duct smoke detector. See costs[].

source.title: 2024 Building Code Compendium (MMAH), Division B

relatedSources.section: 9.33.1.1.(2) (systems serving more than one dwelling unit designed to Part 6)

relatedSources.title: Add a second unit to your house
relatedSources.section: Heating and ventilation (duct-type smoke detector to UL 268A)

rules.notes: The UL 268A detector standard comes from Ontario's 2023 guide (written for the 2012 Code).

rules.title: Sound separation between the homes
rules.plain: Between the two homes, new construction needs STC 50 (or ASTC 47). In a house 5+ years old you can instead meet STC 43 or ASTC 40, or build 150 mm sound-absorbing insulation in the joists, filled stud spaces, resilient channel on one side and at least 12.7 mm drywall on ceilings and both sides of walls.

options: Construction with joist spaces filled with at least 150 mm nominal sound-absorbing material, stud spaces filled with sound-absorbing material, resilient channel on one side at 400 or 600 mm o.c., and at least 12.7 mm gypsum board on ceilings and both sides of walls
Construction providing an STC rating of at least 43
A separating assembly and adjoining constructions together providing an ASTC rating of at least 40

source.title: 2024 Building Code Compendium, Division B Part 11

evidence.question: Is there insulation between the basement ceiling joists now? Are you planning mineral wool, resilient channel and drywall on the ceiling?

fix.description: Fill joist and stud cavities with mineral wool, add resilient channel on one side, then drywall (5/8 in. Type X also covers the fire rule).

costSource.title: Soundproofing Cost Toronto: 2026 Comparison Across Tiers

fix.costNote: Estimate, not a quote. Another source quotes $15-$25/sq ft for a full mineral-wool wall assembly; sources disagree widely (see costs[]).

source.title: 2024 Building Code Compendium (MMAH), Division B

rules.notes: Sentence 9.11.1.1.(2) is 'Reserved' in the Ontario text and 9.11 has no secondary-suite exception, so a house under 5 years old needs STC 50/ASTC 47.

rules.title: Stair headroom: 1,950 mm (1,850 mm under suite beams/ducts)
rules.plain: Stairs serving a house with a secondary suite need at least 1,950 mm clear headroom, measured straight up from the line of the nosings; under beams and ducts in the suite, 1,850 mm.

existingBuildingAlternative.text: Replacement or extension of existing stair systems shall be exempt from the provisions of these Subsections, except that they shall have a minimum width between wall faces of 700 mm and a minimum clear height over tread nosing or landing of 1,800 mm.

source.title: 2024 Building Code Compendium, Division B Part 11

existingBuildingAlternative.interpretationNote: C112 covers replacing or extending a stair. Whether an existing stair left unaltered is accepted as-is falls under Div. A 1.3.3.3C (only altered parts must comply) and is the building department's call.

evidence.scanMeasurement: Vertical clearance from a line through the stair nosings to the lowest point above, over the stair width.
evidence.question: What is the lowest point above the basement stairs, measured straight up from the front edge of the steps?

fix.description: Reframe the opening or bulkhead above the stair or move ducts; not priced in this pack.

source.title: 2024 Building Code Compendium (MMAH), Division B

rules.title: Exit stair width: 860 mm
rules.plain: Exit stairs serving a house with a secondary suite must be at least 860 mm wide.

existingBuildingAlternative.text: Replacement or extension of existing stair systems shall be exempt from the provisions of these Subsections, except that they shall have a minimum width between wall faces of 700 mm and a minimum clear height over tread nosing or landing of 1,800 mm.

source.title: 2024 Building Code Compendium, Division B Part 11

existingBuildingAlternative.interpretationNote: C112 covers replacing or extending a stair. Whether an existing stair left unaltered is accepted as-is falls under Div. A 1.3.3.3C (only altered parts must comply) and is the building department's call.

evidence.scanMeasurement: Clear width of the stair between wall faces (and handrails if they project).
evidence.question: How wide is the basement stair between the walls?

fix.description: Usually only fixable by rebuilding the stair; not priced in this pack.

source.title: 2024 Building Code Compendium (MMAH), Division B

rules.title: Separate ESA electrical permit and inspection
rules.plain: Electrical work for the suite needs its own Electrical Safety Authority (ESA) permit and inspection, separate from the building permit; Ontario recommends a licensed electrical contractor.

evidence.question: Will a licensed electrical contractor take out the ESA permit? Will the suite get its own panel or meter?

fix.description: Hire a licensed electrical contractor to file the ESA notification and wire the suite (circuits, alarms, 3-way stair switches).

costSource.title: How Much Does Basement Development Cost in Canada in 2026?
costSource.note: Read via the r.homestars.com mirror of the same path.

rules.title: Kitchen, bathroom, hot water and its own water shut-off
rules.plain: The suite needs a kitchen sink, a bathroom sink, a toilet and a tub or shower with hot water, access to laundry (it can be shared), a floor drain in its basement, and its own water shut-off valve where the supply enters the unit.

evidence.question: Is there an existing bathroom or a rough-in (capped pipes in the floor) in the basement? Where does the water line enter the house?

fix.description: Add a bathroom (rough-in if none) and a kitchenette, plus a shut-off valve where the supply enters the suite.

costSource.title: Basement Renovation Cost Guide: Kitchener-Waterloo & Cambridge 2026

fix.costNote: Estimate, not a quote, for a full basement bathroom (Waterloo Region). Rough-in alone $8,000-$15,000; kitchenette $7,000-$15,000 (one Toronto source says $20,000-$35,000). See costs[].

rules.title: Minimum room sizes (no minimum unit size in zoning)
rules.plain: Rooms need minimum areas: a bachelor with living, dining, bedroom and kitchen combined at least 13.5 m²; bedrooms 7 m² (one bedroom 9.8 m²) without built-in cabinets; kitchen 4.2 m² (3.7 m² for up to 2 people); living area 13.5 m² (11 m² when combined with kitchen/dining for up to 2 people). Smaller is allowed if shown adequate, for example with built-ins.

evidence.scanMeasurement: Net floor area of each planned room between finished walls (closets excluded).
evidence.question: How many bedrooms do you want in the suite, and roughly how large is the space?

fix.description: Re-plan the layout, combine spaces (combination rooms, 9.5.1.2.) or use built-ins (9.5.1.3.).

rules.title: Already a second home in the house: the Fire Code's minimum
rules.plain: If the house already has two homes, Ontario's Fire Code sets the least it needs: a 30-minute fire separation, or 15 minutes with interconnected smoke alarms, and a safe way out of each home. Plaster or drywall in place on July 14, 1994 counts as 30 minutes.

evidence.question: Is there already a basement apartment in the house?

fix.description: A unit that already exists must at least meet Fire Code Section 9.8. A new unit you build now needs a building permit and follows the Building Code.

source.title: O. Reg. 213/07: Fire Code (consolidation from 2026-01-01)

relatedSources.title: O. Reg. 213/07: Fire Code (consolidation from 2026-01-01)
relatedSources.section: Div. B, 9.1.1.1 (Part 9 is for existing buildings), 9.1.2.2(2) (not for a building that meets the Building Code's fire safety requirements)

rules.notes: Section 9.8 covers a detached, semi-detached or row house with two units, 3 storeys or less and up to 600 m2, where one unit is above the other or they share an interior way out (9.8.1.1). Existing 45 mm solid-core doors with closers are accepted (9.8.2.5(2)).

grants.name: Development charge exemption for a second or third unit in an existing house
grants.amount: Municipal development charges are not charged for a 2nd or 3rd home in an existing detached, semi-detached or row house, or for one home in a building out back.

educationDCs.note: School boards' education development charges follow O. Reg. 20/98, s. 3, which exempts up to 2 additional units in an existing single detached house (1 in a semi or row house) when their gross floor area is no more than the existing unit's.

grants.nextStep: Nothing to apply for. Check the permit bill for any school-board charge.

grants.name: Multigenerational Home Renovation Tax Credit (MHRTC), line 45355
grants.amount: 14% of up to $50,000 of qualifying costs, so up to $7,000, for a suite finished in 2026 or later (the rate follows the lowest federal tax rate, now 14%; the CRA page still shows 2025's 14.5% and $7,250).

conditions.qualifyingIndividual: 65 or older at the end of the tax year, or 18-64 and eligible for the disability tax credit
conditions.qualifyingRelation: 18+; parent, grandparent, child, grandchild, brother, sister, aunt, uncle, niece or nephew of the qualifying individual or their spouse/partner

grants.fitsPlansNote: Only for a suite that lets a senior (65+) or an adult eligible for the disability tax credit live with a qualifying relative. Not for a rental to an unrelated tenant.
grants.nextStep: Keep all receipts and the permit; claim on line 45355 of the tax return for the year the renovation is completed.

process.title: Pick the route
process.detail: Basement finish (still one home) or a second unit (a new home with its own kitchen, bathroom and bedroom). Only the second-unit route brings in the two-household rules: fire separation, interconnected alarms, exits and separate heating.

source.title: Add a second unit in your house (Government of Ontario, updated 2023-01-30)

process.title: Check zoning
process.detail: Ontario stops zoning from banning a second unit on a serviced residential lot, but your municipality's zoning by-law still sets things like parking, entrances and setbacks, and some municipalities license or register second units. Ask its planning or zoning office to confirm in writing.

source.title: Add a second unit in your house (Government of Ontario, updated 2023-01-30)

process.task: Ask your municipality to confirm zoning

process.title: Confirm house age
process.detail: If the house has existed for at least 5 years, Part 11 compliance alternatives (Table 11.5.1.1.-C) can be used instead of some Part 9 rules; newer houses must meet new-construction rules.

source.title: 2024 Building Code Compendium

process.title: Line up money before building
process.detail: CMHC must approve insured financing before construction starts, and most grant programs turn down work that has already begun. Apply first.

source.title: CMHC Refinance for Building Secondary Suites

process.title: Get drawings
process.detail: Construction drawings go with the permit application. An owner may design their own house without registering (Div. C 3.2.5.1.(3)(b)), but ask your building department whether it accepts owner-drawn plans; otherwise a BCIN-registered designer, an architect or an engineer draws them.

source.title: 2024 Building Code Compendium (MMAH), Division C Part 3

relatedSources.title: Add a second unit in your house (Government of Ontario, updated 2023-01-30)

process.title: Apply and pay
process.detail: Apply to your municipality's building department on Ontario's Application for a Permit to Construct or Demolish (the Code requires the Minister's form), with the drawings and the fee your municipality sets. Once the application is complete, the Code gives it 15 business days to issue or refuse a permit for a house with one home above another.

source.title: 2024 Building Code Compendium (MMAH), Division C Part 1
source.section: Division C 1.3.1.2.(2); 1.3.1.3. and Table 1.3.1.3., item 2 (15 days, not counting Saturdays and holidays)

relatedSources.title: Add a second unit in your house (Government of Ontario, updated 2023-01-30)

process.title: ESA electrical permit
process.detail: Electrical work needs a separate ESA permit and inspection, usually filed by a licensed electrical contractor.

source.title: Add a second unit to your house (Government of Ontario)

process.title: Build and book inspections
process.detail: Tell the building department when each stage is ready, before it's covered: footings, framing and ductwork, insulation and vapour barrier, air barrier, fire separations, the plumbing, and completion for occupancy.

process.detail: Before you rent, ask whether your municipality licenses or registers second units. The building department signs off after the final inspection.

registry.termsNote: No registry-specific terms of use were found; the page carries Crown copyright (King's Printer for Ontario).
